questions.text: Per Sec. 810, if a ventilation skylight is used in place of a required window, the glass area of the skylight must be:

options.text: At least 10% of the floor area of the room
Not less than the glass area of the window(s) it replaces
At least 1.00 sq.m. regardless of the window size
Half the area of the window it replaces, since skylights admit more light

questions.rationale: Section 810 is a substitution test — the skylight must provide at least equivalent light-transmitting area to the window it replaces. The skylight may not provide less light or ventilation than the window it substitutes for. If equivalent openable area cannot be achieved through a skylight, 'approved artificial ventilation of equivalent effectiveness' may be used, but the burden of proof rests on the design professional.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 808: rooms without artificial ventilation need window free area of at least 10% of floor area and at least 1.00 sq.m; toilet, bath, laundry, and similar rooms follow the separate 1/20 floor-area rule with a stated absolute minimum; roofed-porch openings require the three Section 808 conditions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 808

questions.text: For a ventilation skylight per Sec. 810, the net free area of the movable sash or louver must be at least equal to:

options.text: The total glass area of the skylight itself, including any fixed panels that do not open
The required openable area of the window(s) it replaces
10% of the room's floor area, calculated based on the net usable space excluding built-in furniture
0.30 sq.m. as a code minimum, which applies regardless of the room's size or function

questions.rationale: Section 810 requires that the movable sash or louver in the skylight provide a net free area not less than the openable area that was required for the replaced window. The free (openable) area of the skylight must match the ventilation capacity of the original window — glass area and free area are separately governed requirements.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 808: rooms without artificial ventilation need window free area of at least 10% of floor area and at least 1.00 sq.m; toilet, bath, laundry, and similar rooms follow the separate 1/20 floor-area rule with a stated absolute minimum; roofed-porch openings require the three Section 808 conditions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 808

questions.text: Per Sec. 811-a, which of the following types of rooms requires artificial ventilation regardless of whether they have direct access to exterior openings or windows?

options.text: Residential kitchens in single-family dwellings
Public toilet rooms in commercial buildings
Industrial or heating equipment rooms
General office rooms in office buildings

questions.rationale: Section 811-a explicitly requires artificial ventilation for rooms housing industrial or heating equipment regardless of other ventilation available. The rationale: such rooms generate heat, combustion products, and pollutant loads that require mechanical extraction — natural ventilation cannot reliably handle the peak loads from equipment operation. This requirement supplements, not replaces, any other applicable ventilation standards.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 808: rooms without artificial ventilation need window free area of at least 10% of floor area and at least 1.00 sq.m; toilet, bath, laundry, and similar rooms follow the separate 1/20 floor-area rule with a stated absolute minimum; roofed-porch openings require the three Section 808 conditions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 808

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Section 808, which of the following statements about the window free area requirement is correct?

options.text: Only the gross window size (frame included) counts toward the 10% requirement, which is calculated based on the total floor area of the room.
Only the free opening area (net area excluding frames, fixed mullions, and non-operable portions) counts toward the 10% requirement
Grilles that block airflow do not reduce the effective free area, provided they are decorative and do not exceed 50% coverage.
The 10% rule applies only to habitable rooms, not to any room without artificial ventilation, unless specified otherwise by local amendments.

questions.rationale: A window with decorative iron grilles, thick frames, and fixed louvered panels might have a gross size of 1.50 sq.m but a free opening of only 0.60 sq.m. The 0.60 sq.m is what counts for ventilation compliance. Architects must specify operable, unobstructed window area — not just nominal opening dimensions.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 808: rooms without artificial ventilation need window free area of at least 10% of floor area and at least 1.00 sq.m; toilet, bath, laundry, and similar rooms follow the separate 1/20 floor-area rule with a stated absolute minimum; roofed-porch openings require the three Section 808 conditions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 808

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Section 808, what is the absolute minimum free area for windows in a room without artificial ventilation, and how does this interact with the percentage-based calculation?

options.text: 1.00 sq.m minimum; the percentage-based calculation always governs regardless of the minimum, ensuring compliance with ventilation standards
1.00 sq.m minimum; if the computed 10% of floor area is less than 1.00 sq.m, use 1.00 sq.m instead
0.50 sq.m minimum; if the computed 10% of floor area is less than 0.50 sq.m, use 0.50 sq.m instead, which is often the case in smaller rooms
2.00 sq.m minimum; no percentage-based calculation applies, making it a straightforward requirement for all room sizes

questions.rationale: The absolute minimum (1.00 sq.m) is the floor, not the target. For a 25.00 sq.m bedroom, 10% × 25.00 = 2.50 sq.m > 1.00 sq.m → use 2.50 sq.m. The 1.00 sq.m only kicks in for very small rooms where 10% of floor area falls below it.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Rule IX, Sec. 905, under what condition must public dining rooms without artificial ventilation be screened?

options.text: All public dining rooms regardless of ventilation type must be screened to ensure compliance with health and safety standards, preventing the entry of pests and maintaining air quality.
Public dining rooms without artificial ventilation must be properly screened
Only dining rooms larger than 50 sq.m require screening, as smaller spaces are considered less susceptible to ventilation issues and pest intrusion.
Only ground-floor dining rooms need to be screened, as they are more exposed to external environmental factors compared to upper floors.

questions.rationale: Per Rule IX, Sec. 905, dining rooms for public use that are without artificial ventilation shall be properly screened. The requirement applies specifically to naturally ventilated public dining spaces to prevent fly-borne contamination.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 811 and Table VIII.4: industrial or heating-equipment rooms require artificial ventilation to prevent excessive hot or polluted air, and required systems must meet the table air-change criteria.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 811 and Table VIII.4

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 808, windows required for light and ventilation must open to which of the following? Which answer is INCORRECT?

options.text: A court, yard, public street, or alley where air and light can freely enter
A qualifying roofed porch that abuts an open space with ceiling height ≥ 2.70 m and ≥ 65% open on the longer side
An enclosed interior corridor between rooms, provided it is air-conditioned
An open watercourse abutting the property where air and light can freely reach the opening

questions.rationale: An enclosed interior corridor — even if air-conditioned — does not constitute a valid opening for required windows under Sec. 808. Windows must open to a court, yard, public street, alley, open watercourse, or a qualifying roofed porch. A window that faces only an enclosed interior corridor provides no path for outdoor air and natural light and therefore cannot satisfy the natural ventilation and light requirements of Rule VIII.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 808: rooms without artificial ventilation need window free area of at least 10% of floor area and at least 1.00 sq.m; toilet, bath, laundry, and similar rooms follow the separate 1/20 floor-area rule with a stated absolute minimum; roofed-porch openings require the three Section 808 conditions.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 808

questions.text: A naturally ventilated master bedroom is 25.00 sq.m; its en-suite bathroom is 4.00 sq.m. Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 808, what are the minimum required free window areas for each room?

options.text: Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.20 sq.m
Bedroom: 1.00 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.24 sq.m
Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.24 sq.m
Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.40 sq.m

questions.rationale: Bedroom: 10% of 25.00 = 2.50 sq.m, which exceeds the 1.00 sq.m absolute minimum, so 2.50 sq.m governs. Bathroom: IRR practice applies 5% rule — 5% of 4.00 = 0.20 sq.m; compare to 0.24 sq.m minimum free area — use the more restrictive 0.24 sq.m. The '240 sq. millimeters' in the printed IRR is a known unit error; professional and PRBoA-annotated practice treats this as 0.24 sq.m.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 806: rooms for human habitation are 6.00 sq.m with 2.00 m least dimension; kitchens are 3.00 sq.m with 1.50 m least dimension; bath/toilet rooms are 1.20 sq.m with 900 mm least dimension.

Habitable: 5.00 sq.m / 2.00 m; Kitchen: 2.50 sq.m / 1.20 m; Bath: 1.00 sq.m / 0.80 m
Habitable: 6.00 sq.m / 2.50 m; Kitchen: 3.00 sq.m / 1.50 m; Bath: 1.50 sq.m / 1.00 m
Habitable: 8.00 sq.m / 2.50 m; Kitchen: 4.00 sq.m / 2.00 m; Bath: 1.50 sq.m / 1.20 m

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 806, the minimum room sizes are: rooms for human habitation (sleeping/living) — 6.00 sq.m floor area, 2.00 m least dimension; kitchens — 3.00 sq.m floor area, 1.50 m least dimension; bath and toilet — 1.20 sq.m floor area, 0.90 m least dimension. The mnemonic '6–3–1.2 / 2–1.5–0.9' (area / least dimension) encodes all six values.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 806: rooms for human habitation are 6.00 sq.m with 2.00 m least dimension; kitchens are 3.00 sq.m with 1.50 m least dimension; bath/toilet rooms are 1.20 sq.m with 900 mm least dimension.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 806

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 805, what are the minimum ceiling heights for rooms with natural ventilation, rooms with artificial ventilation, and mezzanine floors?

options.text: Natural: 2.70 m; Artificial: 2.40 m; Mezzanine: 1.80 m clear above and below
Natural: 2.40 m; Artificial: 2.70 m; Mezzanine: 1.50 m clear above and below
Natural: 2.70 m; Artificial: 2.70 m; Mezzanine: 1.80 m clear above and below
Natural: 2.50 m; Artificial: 2.40 m; Mezzanine: 2.00 m clear above and below

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 805: rooms with natural ventilation require 2.70 m minimum ceiling height on all floors; rooms with artificial ventilation require 2.40 m; mezzanine floors require 1.80 m clear height above and below. The higher minimum for naturally ventilated rooms reflects the need for adequate air-exchange volume through stack effect. You cannot apply the lower 2.40 m standard to naturally ventilated rooms.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VII Section 707 and Table VII.2: BHL is measured from established grade, is subject to stricter zoning/RROW/site/airport controls, and narrow single-RROW caps or sloping-grade rules may control over the occupancy table.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 807, what is the minimum air space per person for school rooms, workshops/factories/offices, and habitable sleeping rooms?

options.text: School: 3.00 cu.m; Workshop/office: 12.00 cu.m; Habitable: 14.00 cu.m
School: 5.00 cu.m; Workshop/office: 15.00 cu.m; Habitable: 20.00 cu.m
School: 3.00 cu.m; Workshop/office: 10.00 cu.m; Habitable: 12.00 cu.m
School: 4.00 cu.m; Workshop/office: 12.00 cu.m; Habitable: 16.00 cu.m

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 807, the minimum air space per person is: school rooms — 3.00 cu.m; workshops, factories, and offices — 12.00 cu.m; habitable rooms (sleeping/living) — 14.00 cu.m. Mnemonic: '3–12–14: School, Work, Home.' School rooms have the smallest requirement because students occupy them for defined short periods; habitable rooms have the largest because occupants spend extended overnight hours in them.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 807: school rooms require 3.00 cu.m plus 1.00 sq.m floor area per person; workshops, factories, and offices require 12.00 cu.m per person; habitable rooms require 14.00 cu.m per person.
questions.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule VIII Section 807

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 808, a window may open into a roofed porch instead of directly to a yard or street. Which THREE conditions must ALL be satisfied?

options.text: Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.70 m; at least 65% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts a property line; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.40 m; at least 50% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.70 m; at least 50% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.40 m; at least 65% of the longer side is open and unobstructed

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 808, windows may open to a roofed porch only when ALL three conditions are met: (1) the porch abuts a court, yard, public street, alley, or open watercourse; (2) porch ceiling height is at least 2.70 m; (3) at least 65% of the longer side of the porch is open and unobstructed. Failing any single condition invalidates the exception.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 804, what are the minimum horizontal dimension of any court and the minimum width of a passageway to an inner court?

options.text: Minimum court dimension: 1.20 m; minimum passageway: 0.90 m
Minimum court dimension: 2.00 m; minimum passageway: 1.20 m
Minimum court dimension: 2.00 m; minimum passageway: 0.90 m
Minimum court dimension: 1.50 m; minimum passageway: 1.20 m

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 804, the minimum horizontal dimension of any court is 2.00 m, and the minimum width of a passageway to an inner court is 1.20 m. A court less than 2.00 m in its least dimension is non-compliant even if its total area appears adequate. The least dimension control is explicit. The alternative to a passageway is access via a door through one or more rooms.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 804 and Tables VIII.2-VIII.3: use the correct occupancy/RROW table, keep courts and yards distinct, and apply the 300 mm side/rear court increment only for buildings more than two storeys up to the fourteenth storey.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 809, what are the minimum cross-sectional area and minimum least dimension required for a vent shaft?

options.text: 1.00 sq.m per meter of height (never less than 1.00 sq.m total); least dimension 600 mm
0.30 sq.m per meter of height (never less than 0.30 sq.m total); least dimension 300 mm
2.00 sq.m per meter of height (never less than 2.00 sq.m total); least dimension 900 mm
1.00 sq.m per meter of height (never less than 1.00 sq.m total); least dimension 300 mm

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 809, the minimum cross-sectional area of a vent shaft is 1.00 sq.m per meter of shaft height, but never less than 1.00 sq.m total. The minimum least dimension of the shaft is 600 mm. Air ducts within the shaft have smaller minimums: 0.30 sq.m cross-sectional area and 300 mm least dimension, with the duct outlet at least 300 mm above street or court level.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 806: rooms for human habitation are 6.00 sq.m with 2.00 m least dimension; kitchens are 3.00 sq.m with 1.50 m least dimension; bath/toilet rooms are 1.20 sq.m with 900 mm least dimension.

questions.text: A factory floor measures 20 m × 15 m with a 4.00 m ceiling. Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 807, what is the maximum number of workers that may legally occupy this space?

options.text: 100 workers — based on 12 cu.m per person for workshops and factories
85 workers — based on 14 cu.m per person for habitable rooms
60 workers — based on 3 cu.m per person for school rooms
300 workers — based on 4 cu.m per person for general occupancies

questions.rationale: Factory floor area = 20 × 15 = 300 sq.m. Volume = 300 × 4.00 = 1,200 cu.m. Per Sec. 807, workshops and factories require 12.00 cu.m per person. Maximum occupancy = 1,200 / 12 = 100 workers. The habitable-room standard of 14 cu.m (Answer B) does not apply to factory floors; the school-room standard of 3 cu.m (Answer C) applies only to classrooms.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 805: natural ventilation requires 2.70 m; artificial ventilation requires 2.40 m; multi-storey/headroom and mezzanine clearances must be checked separately.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 808, eaves, canopies, awnings, and similar projecting elements over required window openings must be at what minimum distance from side and rear property lines?

options.text: At least 300 mm from side and rear property lines
At least 600 mm from side and rear property lines
At least 750 mm from side and rear property lines
At least 1,200 mm from side and rear property lines

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 808, projecting elements such as eaves, canopies, awnings, and media aguas over required window openings must be at least 750 mm from side and rear property lines. This clearance ensures the projecting overhang does not block light and ventilation reaching neighboring properties and prevents the overhang from effectively sealing off the required window opening.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 808, a window may open into a roofed porch instead of directly to a yard or street. Which THREE conditions must ALL be satisfied?

options.text: Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.70 m; at least 65% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts a property line; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.40 m; at least 50% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.70 m; at least 50% of the longer side is open and unobstructed
Porch abuts an open space; porch ceiling height ≥ 2.40 m; at least 65% of the longer side is open and unobstructed

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 808, windows may open to a roofed porch only when ALL three conditions are met: (1) the porch abuts a court, yard, public street, alley, or open watercourse; (2) porch ceiling height is at least 2.70 m; (3) at least 65% of the longer side of the porch is open and unobstructed. Failing any single condition invalidates the exception.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Sec. 804, what are the minimum horizontal dimension of any court and the minimum width of a passageway to an inner court?

options.text: Minimum court dimension: 1.20 m; minimum passageway: 0.90 m
Minimum court dimension: 2.00 m; minimum passageway: 1.20 m
Minimum court dimension: 2.00 m; minimum passageway: 0.90 m
Minimum court dimension: 1.50 m; minimum passageway: 1.20 m

questions.rationale: Per Sec. 804, the minimum horizontal dimension of any court is 2.00 m, and the minimum width of a passageway to an inner court is 1.20 m. A court less than 2.00 m in its least dimension is non-compliant even if its total area appears adequate. The least dimension control is explicit. The alternative to a passageway is access via a door through one or more rooms.
questions.explanation: Source-audited against Rule VIII Section 804 and Tables VIII.2-VIII.3: use the correct occupancy/RROW table, keep courts and yards distinct, and apply the 300 mm side/rear court increment only for buildings more than two storeys up to the fourteenth storey.
